text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Russia's foreign minister Jevgenij Primakov said on Saturday that his country continues to object strongly to the Baltic countries' bid for NATO membership and that alternative security guarantees might be offered to them.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas leaves to Estonia on Monday to meet the presidents of Estonia, Latvia, Ukraine and Poland.
- The Lithuanian government intends to raise the prices on alcohol trade lisences to 500,000 litas from 350,000 litas. Two companies in Lithuania say they can afford the sum.

- Lithuania's Free Independent Channel controls 44.57 percent of the country's TV adverising market followed by National TV with 26.68 percent, Tele-3 with 21.34 percent and Baltijos TV with 7.41 percent.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas will meet Pope John Paul II on June 3 in Poland together with the presidents of Poland, Germany, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia.
- Lithuanian Railways has asked the government to raise prices on passenger transportation to nine cents per kilometer since the company suffers losses from this activity.
- Creditantstalt Investment Bank intends to open its representative office in Vilnius in a few months.
- Electronic producer Vilniaus Vingis boosted its sales by 30 percent in the first four months of the year versus the same period in 1996.
- The Bank of Lithuania said that it might launch repo auctions at the beginning of June.
- The Lithuanian - Swedish company Genchiu Oil extracted 84,000 tonnes of crude oil in 1996 and plans to expand its activities.
- A joint Belgium-French-Dutch company, Distace ABC1, intends to construct an entertainment park in Vilnius.
